summary.en: Security forces used drones and CCTV to stop a terrorist attack in Riyom, while gunmen killed a traditional ruler in Plateau and murdered four vigilantes there. In Plateau, gunmen also stormed a mining site, killing two people, and killed a monarch at his home. Bandits besieged a Kaduna estate, forcing residents to flee, and abducted a pregnant woman, her husband and their six-month-old daughter, demanding a large ransom. Catholic priest John Otache was abducted in Benue, prompting police deployment for his rescue. A nurse died after an asthma attack at a federal hospital amid claims of emergency care failures. The conflict produced 1,486 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

background.title: Boko Haram insurgency
background.extract: The Boko Haram insurgency began in July 2009, when the militant Islamist and jihadist rebel group Boko Haram started an armed rebellion against the government of Nigeria. Boko Haram targets both Muslims and Christians. Attacks are often directed at individuals perceived as supporting the Nigerian government or Islamic State after the split between them, including civil servants, local defense groups, Muslim leaders who oppose the group and other rebels like al-Qaeda and Islamic State. Most attacks are not based on the religion of the victims.
